plainTranslation:
This person may reflect something important back to you, but it can be difficult to tell what is real and what is projection.

There is often a strong attraction here that is hard to ignore. The connection may feel romantic, spiritual, creative, or simply important from the very beginning. The Neptune person may quickly feel that the Sun person has a special place in their life, even before they truly know them. The Sun person may feel captivated by the Neptune person's mystery, imagination, or emotional depth, yet find themselves wondering what is actually happening between them and where the relationship is headed.

When this aspect is working well, each person helps the other grow in a meaningful way. The Neptune person often encourages the Sun person to trust their imagination, follow their inspiration, and see themselves as more than the roles or labels they have outgrown. The Sun person, in turn, helps the Neptune person turn hopes and dreams into something real. Instead of leaving ideas floating in the realm of possibility, they encourage action, expression, and follow-through. Together, they can create a relationship that feels both inspiring and grounded, where dreams are not just imagined but actually lived.

Oppositions invite projection. Each person can start relating to an image instead of the person. The Sun person may become the answer, while the Neptune person becomes the dream. Over time, it gets harder to tell what is real and what is imagined. This connection is healthiest when both people allow the illusion to fall away and get to know each other as they truly are. The attraction often grows in the space between what is known and what is imagined. Each person may begin filling in the missing pieces with hopes, assumptions, or longings of their own. When reality eventually challenges those expectations, the letdown can feel surprisingly intense. Neither person may have intended to create an illusion, yet both can end up feeling confused by the difference between what they believed and what was actually there.

The invitation here is to keep returning to the person in front of you. Ask yourself what is actually true. Notice where you are filling in the blanks. Disappointment is not always a sign that something has gone wrong. Sometimes it is simply the moment when reality arrives and asks to be included. This connection can be deeply beautiful when both people allow room for mystery without abandoning truth.
